title: Decision: pending() as non-Unix SIGTERM arm
description: signal.rs uses std::future::pending::<()>() as the SIGTERM branch on non-Unix platforms. tokio::select! requires both arms to be futures with a compatible output type. pending() is a future that never resolves and has output type (), which matches the ctrl_c arm. This is the correct idiom: it compiles without a cfg-gated select! macro and communicates intent (this arm is deliberately inactive) more clearly than a dummy async block or an unreachable channel.
